name: Light Pastel Green
lede: Light Pastel Green is a lightened reading of [[pastel-green|Pastel Green]], one of the crowd-sourced names the xkcd color survey filed in 2010.

sections.title: A modifier on a chalky green
sections.body:
The name is built by grammar: "light" over the parent [[pastel-green|Pastel Green]], itself named for its soft, chalky look rather than for a dye or pigment [1]. Our only record of this exact step is the xkcd color survey of 2010, a crowd-sourced monitor-color study, not a dyer's or naturalist's list [1].

Its nearest named neighbor in the color graph is [[very-light-green|Light Light Green]], 3.1 units away, with [[very-light-green|Light Mint]] close behind at 3.7 [1]. Both read as slightly duller versions of this same pale yellow-green.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds this color covering at least 1 percent of its canvas, within a color distance of 4, as photographed [2]. A bright, pale green this close to a monitor's full saturation sits outside the range of pigments and dyes available to painters working before modern screens [2].

origin.named_after: a descriptive modifier: light + Pastel Green
